body.statement: In the square model \(X=W^{-1}e\), if \(W\) is nonsingular, the coordinates of \(e\) are independent and nondegenerate, and at most one coordinate of \(e\) is Gaussian, then the observational law \(P_X\) determines the monomial row orbit \([W]_{\mathrm{mon}}\).

source.verbatim_statement: The matrix \(A\) can be identified up to scaling and permutation as long as the observed distribution is a linear, invertible mixture of independent components

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:1206.3273, Section 3.1; the same source sentence continues with the at-most-one-Gaussian condition, and Theorem 2 lists nonzero variances and mutual independence.
